It's an amusing article, but after I read this part:

Technician Jørgen Eriksen - Possibly the most complex example of SCP-HR009-J, this personnel file was replaced with an open comment thread, in which dozens of personnel affected by the anomaly proceeded to post incomprehensible, low-information content. This incident was similar to SCP-████, a phenomenon affecting multiple Sites that was ultimately decommissioned by a 13-0 Overseer Council vote after being deemed to have no worthwhile research utility.

I got the sense that this, at least in part, is a disguised vent about titles/author pages/other style-based things that the writer dislikes. Novoting because I can't prove it and may well be biased myself, and it is funny in places, but it feels in bad taste.

As the author with the current longest title on the mainlist, I feel personally attacked by this. no longer the case

+1

When I was ten, I was working on a project in school. As I peered over the project of a partner, I saw the face of beloved Hanna-Barbera character Speedy Gonzalez on the computer screen across from me. Not knowing much about the character, I asked my classmate "Oh, he's from Yogi Bear, right?"

My classmate turned to me and said, "Yogi Bear isn't real."

For the life of me, and to this day, I am still baffled by what he meant by that. While yes, Yogi Bear is not real, how does that reply answer my question? Under what circumstances is Speedy Gonzalez real, while Yogi Bear is not? Did my classmate think that Speedy Gonzalez was a real mouse that lived in Mexico? I struggle with these questions every day of my life, but I do not have the courage to ask him what he meant. It has been far too long, in any case.

I would like to imagine my classmate is the creator of SCP-2000 portrayed in this article.
